top_story.headline: Marshals Service gives Coinbase an $8.1 million no-bid cryptocurrency custody deal after a theft at its previous contractor
top_story.dek: The sole-source justification says the Coinbase award is urgent because the incumbent was ordered to stop work after an employee allegedly stole seized cryptocurrency.
paragraphs: The U.S. Marshals Service plans an 18-month, firm-fixed-price contract with Coinbase Inc. for custody, management and disposal of seized cryptocurrency in its Class 2-4 inventory. The justification puts the estimated value at $8,128,125 and invokes the urgent-need exception, "unusual and compelling urgency." The file name carries a September 14 date; the notice was posted today (notice, justification).

According to the justification, the prior Class 2-4 contract went to Command Services and Support Inc., and an unsuccessful bidder protested that award at the agency level and at the Government Accountability Office without success. The document says a stop-work notice was issued on January 23, 2026, after an employee of that contractor allegedly stole seized cryptocurrency, with a loss of "at least $46 million." The screening pass could not match that passage word for word, so the $46 million figure is a lead, not a verified fact.

The Marshals Service says Coinbase is "the only company with a current Authorization to Use (ATU) designation" that could perform without substantial interruption. The justification adds that such a designation typically takes six months or longer to obtain, per the screening pass, which could not verify that passage verbatim. USAspending shows Coinbase's first federal contract on record in May 2020.

sections.headline: Homeland Security charters shuttles to its St. Elizabeths campus without competition after an event moved
paragraphs: Of 12 items tagged to Washington, D.C., three really belong here: one sole-source justification and two sources-sought notices. Four were moved to their home sections because the capital was only an office address, and five were left out as repeats of notices already listed in earlier editions.

blocks.title: Homeland Security charters shuttles to its St. Elizabeths campus without competition after an event venue changed
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Department of Homeland Security is buying round-trip chartered transportation for its personnel from the Washington, D.C. area to the St. Elizabeths campus for October 27-29, 2026 from Chart Up, LLC. The notice was posted October 27, the first day of service. The justification says the three-day event was originally to be held at a location that did not require transportation, but "due to unforeseen circumstances the event had to be relocated."
Also worth a look

items: Army Corps of Engineers asks industry about a controls and instrumentation purchase agreement for the Washington Aqueduct. The sources-sought notice describes the aqueduct as two treatment plants in the District of Columbia. (W912DR27XC1S4)

Interior Department looks for on-site physical wellness providers for its headquarters at the Stewart L. Udall Building. The industry day and request for information covers 1849 C Street NW. (DOIDSAM270004)

sections.headline: NASA buys Artemis avionics from Space Vector without competition, citing a race with China
paragraphs: There are 29 new sole-source justifications here, plus one in the Washington, D.C. section, and 25 repeats from earlier editions were left out. Thirteen of the day's justifications were posted under other notice types such as award notices, special notices and sources-sought notices. Six of the new ones are extensions or bridges and sit in the Extensions section. The biggest story, the Marshals Service's Coinbase contract, is today's Top Story.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: NASA buys Artemis secondary-payload avionics from Space Vector without competition, citing urgency and a race with China
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration's Marshall Space Flight Center is buying Secondary Payload Avionics Units and engineering support for the Artemis IV and V missions, including a spare, from Space Vector LLC. The units control deployment of secondary payloads from the Space Launch System. The justification says Space Vector designed and built the units that flew on Artemis I and II and that any new supplier would add months, and it cites Executive Order 14369 on returning astronauts to the Moon by 2028. It states: "It is critical to the national interests of the United States... that the Artemis program return American astronauts to the Moon before China reaches this milestone."

blocks.title: Census Bureau sole-sources $950,000 of current and historical voter registration data from Labels & Lists
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The U.S. Census Bureau wants current and historical raw and enhanced voter registration data for all 50 states and the District of Columbia from Labels & Lists Inc. ("L2") for 12 months, to support administrative-records research for the 2027 Census Test and the 2030 Census. The justification says "L2 is the only source capable of providing the specific data set" and that the bureau has historically used L2's enhanced data. USAspending shows the company's earliest federal contract under this name dated October 23, 2026, four days ago.

blocks.title: Air Force gives KBR Wyle a follow-on contract to run Wright-Patterson's centrifuge and altitude chambers without competition
meta: value redacted in the justification; award notice lists $15,000,000
only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Air Force Research Laboratory plans a 60-month indefinite-quantity contract with KBR Wyle Services, LLC to operate and maintain the centrifuge and research altitude chambers at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base. The justification calls the incumbent the only contractor able to do the work without unacceptable risk and says the facility must be running by October 1, 2026. It estimates a competitor's learning curve at $2.1 million to $3.2 million and 12 to 18 months, per the screening pass, which could not verify that quote verbatim. It was posted as an award notice, which lists the award date as September 25.
Also worth a look

sections.headline: Air Force extends RC-135 aircrew training contract six months without competition, blaming the shutdown and DOGE-driven changes
paragraphs: Six new extensions or bridges, none of them repeats. Two Federal Bureau of Prisons medical bridges, an Air Force training extension, a General Services Administration lease and two Transportation Security Administration airport screening extensions.

blocks.title: Air Force extends its RC-135 aircrew training contract six months without competition after the recompete slipped
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Air Force's Air Combat Command extends contract FA4890-21-C-0001 for RC-135 aircrew training and courseware at Offutt Air Force Base, Nebraska, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027. The Air Force had already used a six-month services extension on April 1, 2026, which runs through October 31. The justification blames the October-November 2025 government shutdown and "requirement changes due to DOGE feedback" for delaying the recompete, now expected to be awarded February 1, 2027. It says current work cannot be competed in the time left.

blocks.title: Federal Bureau of Prisons keeps Naphcare running Brooklyn jail medical care without competition while a protest holds up a new contract
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Federal Bureau of Prisons will buy a month of comprehensive medical services for the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn from the incumbent Naphcare, for an estimated $889,017.86 covering October 1 through 31, 2026, though the notice was posted October 27. The justification says "Award of a CMS contract is pending the resolution of a protest." It says the incumbent has served the institution for over five years and that a new provider would need 30 or more days to credential staff and 60 days for security clearances. The pipeline logged an earlier Naphcare justification for $555,000 at the Petersburg prison complex.
Other extensions

items: Federal Bureau of Prisons keeps Integrated Medical Services providing medical care at FCI Sheridan, Oregon, through December without competition. The estimated cost is $810,410. (15B61226P00000144)

Transportation Security Administration extends airport security screening at Rochester's Frederick Douglass Greater Rochester International Airport without competition. No value is given. (JA-2026-05-1400)

sections.headline: Defense Logistics Agency awards six medical-surgical prime vendor contracts with a combined ceiling near $22 billion
paragraphs: Of 434 new award notices, 50 repeats were left out and one flagged notice sits in the Washington, D.C. parts. The prime vendor awards below dominate the day; most others are Defense Logistics Agency parts buys.

blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency picks Cardinal Health, McKesson and Concordance for ten-year medical supply contracts
blocks.text: The Defense Logistics Agency awarded fixed-price, indefinite-quantity Medical Surgical Prime Vendor contracts to Cardinal Health 200, LLC, McKesson Medical-Surgical Government Solutions LLC and Concordance Healthcare Solutions LLC. Each has a 30-month base and three 30-month options, ending June 6, 2037. The notices name the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Defense Health Agency, Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Health and Human Services as customers. The amounts are maximum values:

North back-up: Concordance Healthcare Solutions LLC, $982,264,244 (SPE2DV27D0002)
South primary: McKesson Medical-Surgical Government Solutions LLC, $4,368,779,534 (SPE2DV27D0003)
South backup: Cardinal Health 200, LLC, $485,419,948 (SPE2DV27D0004)
West primary: Cardinal Health 200, LLC, $6,573,132,798 (SPE2DV27D0005)
West backup: Concordance Healthcare Solutions LLC, $730,348,089 (SPE2DV27D0006)

meta: BAE Systems Maritime Solutions Jacksonville LLC
blocks.text: Naval Sea Systems Command awarded BAE Systems Maritime Solutions Jacksonville LLC a firm-fixed-price contract for maintenance, modernization and repair of USS St. Louis (LCS 19) in a fiscal 2027 Docking Selected Restricted Availability. The notice says it was competed with full and open competition. Options would bring the cumulative value to $80,693,639. It was tagged to Washington, D.C. only because the contracting activity is listed there.
Also worth a look

sections.headline: Army Corps of Engineers seeks bids for a Puerto Rico flood control project estimated at $250 million to $350 million
paragraphs: Of 244 new solicitations, 139 repeats were left out and three flagged ones are in the Washington, D.C. parts.

blocks.title: Army Corps of Engineers seeks a builder for the Rio de la Plata flood control project in Dorado and Toa Baja, Puerto Rico
meta: $250 million to $350 million per the notice
blocks.text: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers will award one firm-fixed-price design-bid-build construction contract. The notice says the estimated magnitude is between $250,000,000 and $350,000,000, while a June site-visit presentation lists $300,000,000 to $400,000,000. The notice warns that "all real estate rights have not yet been obtained" for access to the full site.

blocks.title: Federal Bureau of Prisons seeks secure juvenile detention beds in Garza County, Texas
blocks.text: The Federal Bureau of Prisons wants a contractor for secure in-house juvenile services for male and female federal juvenile offenders, with a guaranteed minimum of 13 beds and an estimated maximum of 20. It is an indefinite-quantity contract with fixed unit prices, a one-year base and four one-year options. All 18 attached files are queued for reading.

blocks.title: Grand Canyon South Rim wastewater plant replacement is advertised as an unfunded requirement
blocks.text: The National Park Service solicitation for replacing the wastewater plant at South Rim Village says it is "currently an unfunded requirement with a high expectation that funds will be available," and that a contract will be awarded "when and if funds become available." An answers-to-questions amendment says the contractor must operate the new treatment facilities for 12 months. A specification amendment loosens the maximum water content of washed grit from 10 percent to 40 percent.

items: Navy posts the formal request for proposals for E-6B Mercury depot overhaul work. It plans one indefinite-quantity contract with a five-year ordering period and a five-year option, and calls it single-source even as it cites full and open competition. (N0001927R1025)

sections.headline: Immigration agency seeks packaged meals three times a day for its Atlanta detention intake unit
paragraphs: Of 427 new combined notices, 107 repeats were left out and one flagged notice is in the Washington, D.C. parts.

blocks.title: Immigration and Customs Enforcement seeks individually packaged meals for its Atlanta detention intake unit
blocks.text: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement wants a small-business vendor to deliver individually packaged breakfast, lunch and dinner seven days a week to the Atlanta Field Office's Detention Intake Processing Unit. The notice cites a statement of work; its five attached files are queued for reading.

blocks.title: Border Patrol seeks 15 detection canines and 3 patrol canines for its El Paso K9 Center
blocks.text: U.S. Customs and Border Protection posted three requests for quotes for its Border Patrol K9 Center in El Paso: two for 15 untrained detection canines each and one for three dual-purpose patrol canines. It can buy more if funds are available.

blocks.text: The Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service wants to buy and store foot and mouth disease vaccine antigen concentrate, convert government-owned concentrate into usable vaccine and buy finished vaccine. It is unrestricted. All five attachments are queued.

sections.headline: Space Force plans a sole-source satellite sustainment contract with Boeing worth up to about $945.9 million
paragraphs: Of 100 new presolicitations, 56 repeats were left out. Three stand out; most of the rest are Navy and Defense Logistics Agency parts.

blocks.title: Space Force plans a sole-source satellite sustainment contract with Boeing worth up to about $945.9 million
blocks.text: The U.S. Space Force's Space Systems Command intends a sole-source indefinite-quantity contract with The Boeing Company for Wideband and Narrowband Global SATCOM Sustainment. The ceiling is about $945.9 million: $480.6 million for a five-year base ordering period and $465.3 million for a ten-year option. It covers engineering, sustainment, cybersecurity and modernization across several military satellite communications constellations.

blocks.title: Defense Information Systems Agency plans to keep By Light running its fiber network without competition while the competed follow-on is set up
blocks.text: The Defense Information Systems Agency intends to award a sole-source contract to the current contractor, By Light Professional IT Services LLC, by November 30, 2026, for operation and maintenance of dark fiber. The notice says this prevents a lapse "while transition to the follow-on contract, which was competitively awarded, is completed."

blocks.title: Army plans a sole-source Motorola Solutions radio buy of more than 37,000 units
blocks.text: Army Contracting Command-Aberdeen Proving Ground intends a sole-source firm-fixed-price contract with Motorola Solutions, Inc. for 34,950 portable VHF radios, 2,100 portable UHF radios and a mobile VHF quantity that the notice prints both as "six hundred ninety" and as 10,690. It supports the Communications-Electronics Command's security assistance work.

sections.headline: Missile Defense Agency awards Raytheon a $745 million noncompetitive deal for Standard Missile-3 rounds
paragraphs: Of 52 new special notices, 36 repeats were left out and one flagged notice is in the Washington, D.C. parts.

blocks.title: Missile Defense Agency awards Raytheon a noncompetitive $745 million contract for Standard Missile-3 Block IIA rounds
blocks.text: The Missile Defense Agency is awarding Raytheon in Tucson an undefinitized contract action to build Standard Missile-3 Block IIA all-up rounds for the U.S. and Japan's Ministry of Defense. Funds obligated at award are $275,613,909 in fiscal 2026 procurement money and $277,688,036.35 from Japan; work runs to February 28, 2031. The text is headed "07 August Contract Announcement," though the notice posted October 27.

blocks.title: Army Corps of Engineers previews a design-build competition for the 91st Cyber Operations Center
blocks.text: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Fort Worth District announced a competition for the 91st Cyber Operations Center using progressive design-build under other-transaction authority for construction, 10 U.S.C. 2808a. It is a qualifications-based, two-phase approach. The six attached files are queued.

sections.headline: Secret Service asks industry how it would run transportation for National Special Security Events
paragraphs: Of 124 new sources-sought notices, 71 repeats were left out and five flagged ones are in the Washington, D.C. parts.

blocks.title: Secret Service seeks industry input on event transportation logistics for National Special Security Events
blocks.text: The U.S. Secret Service is asking industry about capabilities to provide event transportation logistics coordination for National Special Security Events. Amendment 1 posted answers to industry questions. It is a request for information only.

blocks.title: Transportation Department's Volpe Center asks about refurbished boxcars for ammunition and explosives
blocks.text: The Volpe National Transportation Systems Center is researching refurbished and used boxcars, which its request says are "needed to safely transport ammunition and explosives in compliance with strict military safety regulations." Cars would be delivered to a continental U.S. Army rail base, "location TBD." The deadline was extended from October 21.

sections.headline: No new USAspending contract actions cleared the featured thresholds today
paragraphs: From this morning's edition: USAspending.gov is pulled once a day.
No new awards of $2 million or more, large modifications or cuts were featured, and none were moved to the White House or D.C. sections.

blocks.text: Under $2 million: 5 new awards screened, 1 from the Defense backlog, none flagged (Veterans Affairs 2, General Services Administration 2, Defense Department 1).

sections.headline: No new apportionment files or spend-plan changes in this window
paragraphs: The Treasury Department did not release any new apportionment files between October 22 and October 27. No federal agencies filed updates to their spending plans or submitted modifications that match the tracking keywords monitored for this section.

footer.coverage_window: October 26-27, 2026 (Pacific time), SAM.gov notices and justifications posted since the morning edition.
footer.sources: OMB apportionment data via openomb.org and apportionment-public.max.gov; SAM.gov contract opportunities and their attached documents. USAspending was not pulled in this PM edition by design; the morning's section is carried in.
footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported. The OMB Apportionments pass found no new apportionment files or spend-plan changes. Document coverage: 2,283 files on 464 notices were in scope; 139 are access-restricted on SAM.gov, 1 could not be downloaded or read, and 1,372 are queued for a later edition (5,391 files overall are queued), while 13 failed during this run's reading. About 1,150 links to outside portals, mostly DIBBS, NECO and PIEE, were not followed. Findings marked unverified are leads, not confirmed facts.
